abstract: This paper researches a next-generation ultrahigh-definition television (UHDTV) broadcasting system. The video parameters of UHDTV systems with 120 frame/sec signals are specified in the Recommendation of the International Telecommunications Union Radiocommunication Sector, broadcasting service (television) series 2020. In this study, a new mapping method was developed to transmit various UHDTV signals, including 120 frame/sec signals. A prototype interface for connecting UHDTV video devices was also developed. The method is to transform UHDTV signals into multilink 10 Gbit/sec streams. The number of 10 Gbit/sec streams differs according to the UHDTV format (frame frequency, pixel count, and sampling lattice). To realize a compact and low-power interface, the prototype using a parallel fiber-optic transceiver with a capacity of 10 Gbit/sec per channel was implemented. Finally, the practicality and feasibility of the multilink 10 Gbit/sec mapping method and the prototype interface was verified.

authors.bio: Takuji Soeno is a research engineer in the Advanced Television Systems Research Division, at NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corp.) Science and Technology Research Laboratories. He received B.E. and M.E. degrees from Keio University in 2002 and 2004, respectively. In 2004, he joined NHK and built his career as a video engineer through television program production. Since 2010, Soeno has been in charge of the research and development of ultrahigh-definition television systems, particularly camera, image sensor, and digital signal processing. He is a member of the Institute of Image Information and Television Engineers of Japan (ITE).
authors.name: Takuji Soeno

authors.bio: Yukihiro Nishida is a senior research engineer in the Advanced Television Systems Research Division, at NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories. He has been involved in many areas of broadcasting technologies including HDTV, digital broadcasting, video coding, multiplexing, quality evaluation, and UHDTV. He is also active in the standardization of broadcast technologies in ITU-R and ARIB. Nishida is vice-chair of ITU-R Study Group 6 on broadcasting services, and is also chair of Working Party 6B. He received B.S. and M.S. degrees in electric engineering from Keio University and a Ph.D. in engineering from the University of Electro-Communications.
authors.name: Yukihiro Nishida

authors.bio: Takayuki Yamashita is a senior research engineer at NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories. He is working on the research of ultrahigh-definition television systems and his research fields include the development of camera systems, image sensors and high-bandwidth digital signal processing. He also has an interest in the research of capturing system for next-generation 3DTV. Yamashita joined NHK in 1995 after receiving B.E. and M.E. degrees in electronic engineering and information science from Kyoto Institute of Technology in 1993 and 1995, respectively. He has been engaged in research of HDTV camera systems since 1999. He is a member of SMPTE and ITE.
authors.name: Takayuki Yamashita

authors.bio: Yuichi Kusakabe received B.E and M.S. degrees in applied physics from the University of Tokyo. In 1999, he joined NHK, where he is a principal research engineer in the Science and Technology Research Laboratories. He is currently engaged in the development of display systems for ultrahigh-definition television, especially projectors and LCDs. He has been active in a working party in ARIB that deals with UHDTV interfaces. Kusakabe is a member of ITE.
authors.name: Yuichi Kusakabe

authors.bio: Ryohei Funatsu joined NHK in 2002. Since 2004, he has been engaged in research of ultrahigh-definition TV camera systems at NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories. His research interests include the development of high-resolution image sensor and the high-performance signal processing. He received B.E. and M.E. degrees in electrical and electronic engineering from Tokyo Institute of Technology in 2000 and 2002, respectively. He is a member of ITE.
authors.name: Ryohei Funatsu

authors.bio: Tomohiro Nakamura joined NHK in 2008 and has been engaged in the research of UHDTV camera systems at NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories, since 2012. His interest are in the development of UHDTV camera systems. Nakamura received B.S. and M.S. degrees in electrical engineering from Waseda University on 2006 and 2008, respectively. He is a member of ITE.
authors.name: Tomohiro Nakamura
